rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test the core hypothesis of multimodal modeling. This configuration tests multimodal (RNA + image) with singleprofile, using pca_n2000 and resnet50 encoders with simple concatenation fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal integration while keeping other factors minimal, providing foundational insights into whether combining modalities improves performance.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. Since fusion is a critical design choice in multimodal models, this comparison provides direct insight into its impact while keeping other parameters constant, balancing exploration and exploitation efficiently.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.52 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested) while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method consistent. It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical for multimodal cellular profiling, and balances exploration of multiprofile with minimal changes to proven components.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieves high validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion in the same setup improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It isolates the effect of fusion type while keeping other key design choices (multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool) consistent, providing actionable insights with minimal change.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, weighted fusion, and avgpool aggregation significantly improve performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) further enhances accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA representation choice while keeping other parameters aligned with the current best configuration (config_019).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (while keeping other parameters the same) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests the effect of using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same setup, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly compares two critical design choices (fusion method) within a proven high-performing framework, balancing exploitation of existing success with exploration of key hyperparameters.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether the RNA-only setup with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) can match this performance, isolating the necessity of image data. It clarifies if the multimodal success relies on image modality or if RNA representation alone suffices, addressing a key design choice with minimal changes from previous high-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows that using multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_038/039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (a more complex model) further improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It leverages the current best setup while exploring a critical design decision with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of known strengths and exploration of potential improvements.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_038) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a different architecture) in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. This addresses a key design decision with potential high impact, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing configuration and exploration of alternative encoders.
